To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) increasing freshwater inputs to tidal freshwater marshes may be a useful management strategy to mitigate some of the effects of saltwater intrusion, 2) elevated salinity may reduce the capacity of tidal freshwater marsh ecosystems to accumulate organic matter, and 3) ecosystem level responses to saltwater intrusion are highly site-specific.
tidal freshwater marshes may not be able to keep up with sea level rise as saltwater intrudes and freshwater inputs are reduced.
tidal freshwater marshes experiencing saltwater intrusion and altered hydrology have decreased plant productivity and increased rates of soil respiration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impacts of saltwater intrusion, which may be the result of rising sea level, on the ecosystem functioning of tidal freshwater marsh ecosystems.
how the hydrology of tidal freshwater marsh ecosystems responds to changes in sea level, salinity and hydroperiod, and how this response impacts ecosystem processes, productivity and soil elevation.
the effects of saltwater intrusion on ecosystem functioning and how marsh plants, soil biota, and soil processes respond to changes in salinity and hydrologic inputs in a tidal freshwater marsh.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

tidal freshwater marshes are highly sensitive to changes in salinity and hydrologic inputs and these ecosystem changes may be important to the sustainability of tidal freshwater ecosystems in the face of sea level rise and altered precipitation patterns.
elevated salinity has a more significant impact on plant production, whereas increased freshwater inputs have a greater impact on soil respiration.

tidal freshwater marshes are resilient to changes in salinity and water level, but that the magnitude of the response is highly variable and depends on the species composition, soil characteristics, and the duration of the disturbance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of elevated salinity and increasing freshwater inputs on ecosystem level processes are not linearly related and depend on the timing of the manipulation and the magnitude of the change.

tidal freshwater marshes have the capacity to respond to environmental change by altering their internal structure and function, but that these responses may not be sufficient for long term persistence of these ecosystems.

tidal freshwater marshes can respond to changes in salinity and hydrologic inputs by changing the balance of ecosystem processes, which could impact the ability of tidal freshwater marsh to maintain elevation in response to rising sea levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tidal freshwater marshes are dynamic ecosystems that are highly sensitive to changes in water quality and hydrology.
marshes are highly sensitive to changes in salinity and hydrological conditions.
the response of tidal freshwater marsh ecosystems to environmental change is complex and cannot be predicted by simply measuring the response of individual plants to salinity and hydrologic stress.
